summary: Practise WCAG testing, procurement reviews, remediation, and governance for public-facing services. Explore the course and plan team training.
lede: Digital accessibility implementation helps public-service and NGO teams assess and improve websites, forms, and documents. It covers applying WCAG 2.2 and ISO 30071-1, testing keyboard and screen-reader access, and reviewing supplier evidence for procurement. Participants practise prioritising defects, remediating interfaces and documents, and setting up workflows that assign fixes and verify results, with human review of automated findings.
audienceIntro: This course is for professionals responsible for making public-facing digital services usable, testable, and maintainable across organisational teams and suppliers.
prerequisites: Prior experience working with digital services, web content, procurement, service design, IT, or public-facing communications is useful. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop if you want to practise browser-based accessibility checks; specific software access may depend on your organisation's device policies.
